# POC realignment plan

Scribl showed us their own vision. Two sources landed on 2026-08-19/20. First, the
client's sales deck ("Bounteous x Scribl D2C App Presentation", 11 pages), which
carries the brand system. Second, Figma frames for the invite-and-onboarding flow
and the drawing screens, received as 23 PNG exports and committed to this repo at
`product/design/figma-exports/`. The POC at hs2studio/scribl-app was built before
either existed and diverges from both. This plan retunes the POC toward the
client's vision ahead of the next design conversation.

This document is the whole brief for the implementation agent. That agent has not
seen the deck or the Figma file. Every color, screen, and file named here is
traced to a source. POC paths are relative to the scribl-app repo root. Deck
citations are by page (p1..p11). Figma citations name the export file in
`product/design/figma-exports/`.

Two source-quality notes the implementer must respect.

- The deck is the visual-theme truth. Its app mockups (p1, p9) are fully styled.
- The Figma frames are flow truth, not visual truth. They are wireframes on a
  `#1E1E1E` ground with unstyled white outline buttons. Do not copy their dark
  chrome as the app theme without the design call in section 6 being made.
- The Figma prototype was walked end to end in a logged-in browser session
  (22 steps, screenshots captured per step), so the screen order in section 3 is
  the prototype's own order, not an inference.

### Typography

Embedded in the deck (pdffonts): Nunito (ExtraLight, Regular, Bold) and Prompt
(Bold). Arial appears only in footers and small print and is export noise, not
brand.

| Role | Face | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Display / big headlines | Prompt Bold | Deck slide headlines ("Value" p4, "Market" p7, the 94% stats p3) |
| In-app UI, emphasis, subheads | Nunito Bold | Deck p1 mockups; nav titles, prompt questions, CTA labels match Nunito's rounded forms |
| Body | Nunito Regular / ExtraLight | Deck body copy |

In-app ramp, visual estimates from the p1 center phone at iPhone scale: prompt
question ~22-24 pt bold, section header ~20 pt bold, nav title ~17-18 pt bold,
CTA label ~15-16 pt bold, subtitle ~14-15 pt regular muted, comment ~13 pt, meta
and tile author labels ~11-12 pt. Both fonts are on Google Fonts, so
`@expo-google-fonts/nunito` and `@expo-google-fonts/prompt` drop in where
Fredoka and Manrope load today.

### Spacing, radii, icon style

Visual estimates from deck p1 and p9 mockups.

- Buttons are full pills, ~48-52 pt tall, flat `#D51668` fill with white label.
- Cards and drawing tiles are white on `#F8F8FA`, radius ~16-20 pt, soft or no
  shadow, no gradients anywhere.
- Chips are full pills in `#F8F8FA`.
- Icons are thin outlines, ~1.5-2 pt stroke, rounded caps, navy, sitting in
  circular light-gray buttons ~36-40 pt. The filled exception is the heart,
  solid `#D51668` when active.
- Density is airy. Screen margins ~16-20 pt, grid gutters ~12-16 pt, 2-column
  drawing grid on the Family wall (p1), tall ~4:5 tiles.

## 2. Reduced tool set

What their design shows (First Canvas.png, Daily Prompt Blank.png): one brush,
a four-dot size selector across the top (large to small), an undo arrow, six
fixed color swatches, no brush-style choice, no fill tool, no eraser, no clear
button on the canvas.

Note one discrepancy worth naming. The working brief said "one brush at one
size", but the frames clearly show four size dots, and the 2026-08-18 alignment
call said "a couple of brush sizes, one brush". Plan of record is one brush
style with four sizes. Confirm the dot behavior against the prototype.

What the POC has today.

- Four brush styles `basic|fork|dotted|neon` (`packages/shared-types/tools.ts:13`,
  implementations `components/canvas/SkiaCanvas.tsx:62-122`).
- Six sizes `[2,3,5,8,12,18]` (`components/canvas/DrawPad.tsx:13`), size picker
  at `DrawPad.tsx:276-296`, style picker at `DrawPad.tsx:298-317`.
- Sixteen colors (`packages/shared-types/tools.ts:18-38`), swatch UI
  `DrawPad.tsx:251-274`.
- Fill tool (`lib/floodFill.ts`, invoked `SkiaCanvas.tsx:266-307`), Clear and
  Undo (`DrawPad.tsx:134,140`).

Hide, do not delete. The restriction seam already exists: `DrawPad` accepts
`allowedBrushStyles` and `allowedColors` props (`DrawPad.tsx:73,79`), used
today by challenges (`app/create-challenge.tsx`). The challenge feature needs
the full toolset later and is itself deferred (see section 5), so deleting brush
code buys nothing and burns a working seam.

Changes, by file.

1. `packages/shared-types/tools.ts`. Add `REDUCED_PALETTE` with the six inks in
   the order above, and `REDUCED_BRUSH_SIZES = [18, 12, 5, 2]` (largest to
   smallest, matching the dot row; sizes reuse existing tokens, confirm feel on
   device). Keep `PALETTE` and `BRUSH_STYLE_IDS` for the flagged-off full set.
2. `src/config/features.ts`. Add `FULL_TOOLSET = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_FULL_TOOLSET === "1"`,
   default off. The existing `AI_ENABLED` flag in this file is the pattern to
   copy; it is consumed in `app/response/[id].tsx` and
   `components/EnhancedToggleImage.tsx`.
3. `components/canvas/DrawPad.tsx`. When `FULL_TOOLSET` is off, default the
   palette to `REDUCED_PALETTE`, sizes to `REDUCED_BRUSH_SIZES`, force
   `brushStyle = "basic"`, hide the style picker row, hide the fill-mode toggle,
   keep Undo, and move the size dots plus undo to a single top row per First
   Canvas.png (size dots left, undo right, above the canvas; swatches below the
   canvas; prompt pinned in a rounded card at top).
4. `components/canvas/SkiaCanvas.tsx`. No behavior change. Fill stays compiled,
   unreachable without the toggle.
5. `app/create-challenge.tsx`. Gate the whole route behind `FULL_TOOLSET`
   (challenges are not in the first client-facing run per the 2026-08-18
   alignment note and the kickoff board).

The fixed palette is the six inks in section 1. Per-challenge `allowedColors`
still works on top when the flag is on.

## 3. Invite, onboarding, and first-run

### What the POC does today

Routes from `app/` (expo-router single stack, `app/_layout.tsx:84-96`).

- `/` (`app/index.tsx`) redirects to `/sign-up` when no user (lines 44-48).
- `app/sign-up.tsx` is stubbed email+display-name auth with a user-switch list;
  success replaces to `/splash`.
- `app/splash.tsx` is a brand landing with a "Let's start drawing" button.
- `app/tutorial.tsx` is a 3-panel static stepper. No discovered call site
  navigates to it; verify the entry point or treat it as dead.
- There is no invite-accept surface at all. Invites are a server-side email add
  (`src/data/client.ts:185-189`); the invited person signs up with that email
  and the wall is just there. `app.json` sets `"scheme": "scribl"` but nothing
  parses links, and there are no universal-link entitlements.

### The designed flow, screen by screen

Order confirmed by stepping the live prototype in a logged-in browser, 22
screens start to finish. Personalization in the copy ("Hi Sarah",
"Matthew has invited you", "a prompt Matthew chose for you") means the invite
carries inviter and invitee identity into onboarding. That is the core product
difference from our POC, and theirs is better. A guided first-scribble that
lands on the inviter's wall beats our static 3-panel tutorial; it teaches by
doing and pays off the social loop in the first minute.

### Screens that disappear

- `app/tutorial.tsx`, the static 3-panel stepper. Superseded by screens 2-8.
- `app/splash.tsx` as a button-stop. Becomes the animated splash.
- `app/wall.tsx` has no live call site today (`home.tsx` routes group walls to
  `/family`); fold whatever survives into the new wall styling and delete it.
- `app/record.tsx`, the orphaned standalone recorder, replaced by the Record
  path in section 4.
- `app/avatar.tsx` (avatar builder) appears nowhere in the client flow. Keep
  behind `FULL_TOOLSET` or park it; do not spend styling effort on it.

### What the invite flow requires that the POC lacks

The designed flow needs a real invite link. Screen 0 plus "Hi Sarah" implies a
tokenized invite (inviter, wall, invitee name) that survives App Store install.
Full deferred deep linking (install attribution) is heavy; the plan of record is
the light version. Generate an invite URL with a token, backend endpoint
resolves token -> {inviter, wall, prompt}, the app asks "have an invite code?"
on first launch as the fallback when the link did not survive install. Files:
new `app/invite/[token].tsx` route, `backend/lambda/handlers/` new
`invite-create.ts` / `invite-resolve.ts`, `backend/db/schema.sql` new
`invites` table (token, channel_id, inviter_user_id, invitee_email, invitee_name,
expires_at). The share surface (screen 0) is a static page rendered by the
existing share-link pattern (`app/share.tsx` uses `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_BASE_URL`,
which today is "not a real hosted endpoint" per its own comment, line 20). That
hosting gap now matters and is called out in section 5.

## 4. Voice notes

### What the POC records today, established

- Web only. `src/services/audioRecorder.ts` uses browser MediaRecorder over
  `getUserMedia`, blob type hardcoded `audio/webm` (line 40), no bitrate or
  sample-rate config.
- Native recording does not exist. `src/services/audioRecorder.native.ts:10,14`
  throws "Native audio capture deferred to iOS/Android bring-up". No audio
  library is in `package.json` at all.
- Nothing reaches the database. The blob is base64-encoded and POSTed to
  `/transcribe` (`src/services/transcriber.ts:44-85`), a Lambda seam
  (`backend/lambda/handlers/transcribe.ts`) that returns a transcript string
  (stub adapter by default, OpenAI Whisper adapter optional) and discards the
  audio. `backend/db/schema.sql` has zero audio columns. Playback is
  `new window.Audio(uri)` on the in-memory blob, web only, gone on reload.

So "voice notes" in the POC is transcription input, not a stored, replayable
message. The designed feature (Story Input Select.png, "Record your story in 30
seconds or less"; Daily Prompt Blank.png Record button) is a stored voice note
played back from the wall. That is greenfield.

### Target pipeline

Record -> upload raw -> deterministic server-side encode -> store compact ->
replay. No model and no AI anywhere in this path at runtime. Transcription
remains a separate optional seam and is not in the store-replay path.

1. Record. Add `expo-audio` and implement
   `src/services/audioRecorder.native.ts` for real. iOS and Android record AAC
   in an `.m4a` container (the library's high-quality preset), mono, 44.1 kHz.
   Web keeps MediaRecorder webm/Opus. Enforce the 30-second cap client-side
   with a visible countdown (the cap is design-sourced, Story Input Select.png).
2. Upload raw. New handler `backend/lambda/handlers/voice-upload-url.ts`
   returns a presigned S3 PUT URL, key `voice/raw/{responseId}.{ext}`. Client
   uploads the raw file directly, then submits the response referencing the key.
   This replaces the base64-JSON pattern, which pins payloads to API Gateway
   limits.
3. Encode, deterministically. S3 `ObjectCreated` on `voice/raw/` triggers
   `backend/lambda/handlers/voice-encode.ts`, a Lambda carrying a static ffmpeg
   binary as a layer. Fixed arguments, no branching on content:
   `ffmpeg -i {raw} -ac 1 -ar 24000 -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 48k {out}.mp3`.
   A 30-second mono 48 kbps MP3 is ~180 KB worst case. MP3 chosen over AAC for
   universal playback (expo-audio and every browser) with no licensing wrinkles
   in the encoder layer. Output key `voice/notes/{responseId}.mp3`.
4. Store. Schema migration adds to `responses` (or a `voice_notes` table if
   responses stay text-typed): `audio_key`, `audio_status`
   (`uploaded|ready|failed`), `audio_duration_ms`, `audio_bytes`. Files:
   `backend/db/schema.sql`, new migration under `backend/db/migrations/`,
   applied by `backend/scripts/schema-runner.ts`.
5. Raw file disposition. On successful encode, the encode handler deletes the
   raw object. Belt and suspenders, an S3 lifecycle rule expires `voice/raw/`
   at 7 days so failures never accumulate cost.
6. Replay. Client fetches a presigned GET (or CloudFront URL) for
   `voice/notes/{id}.mp3` and plays through expo-audio; wall tiles with voice
   show a play affordance.

Where it runs and what triggers it, stated plainly. The encode runs server-side
in Lambda, triggered by the S3 object-created event after the raw upload
completes. Client-side encode was considered and rejected; ffmpeg-kit for React
Native is retired and heavy, and server-side keeps one deterministic encoder for
all three platforms.

### Failure handling

- Encode failure (corrupt upload, unsupported container) retries via the
  standard async Lambda retry, then lands in a DLQ with a CloudWatch alarm. The
  row stays `audio_status = 'failed'`; the raw file is retained until the
  lifecycle expiry so a fixed encoder can reprocess.
- Client sees `uploaded` as "processing" and `failed` as a re-record prompt.
  Submissions never block on the encode; the drawing and story post regardless.
- Local dev has no S3 events; `backend/local-server.ts` gets a synchronous
  encode call after upload so the pipeline is testable end to end (ffmpeg from
  PATH, same fixed arguments).

### Scope flag, stated plainly

The kickoff board cut voice memos from the MLP (Key Decisions frame, decision 1,
"CUT FROM MLP", reclaiming 1-2 weeks and a native module). The Figma flow the
client just sent puts Record back on both the onboarding story step and the
daily loop. Those two facts conflict. This plan specifies the pipeline so the
work is shovel-ready, but it should not enter a sprint until the client
reconciles their own designs with their own board decision. Raise it in the
design conversation; do not build it silently.

## 6. Where their design and our POC disagree, and which is better

- Guided first-scribble onboarding beats our static tutorial. Theirs wins.
  Adopt fully (items 4-5).
- One brush, six inks beats our 4-brush 16-color 6-size toolbox for this
  product. Theirs wins. The deck's whole visual story is "user drawings carry
  the color"; a constrained crayon set is the brand. Our extra tooling survives
  behind the flag for challenges later.
- Canvas surface color is unresolved. The Figma frames draw on `#1E1E1E`; every
  deck mockup shows drawings on white cards on a paper-light UI, and the indigo
  ink `#20145F` is nearly invisible on dark. My call is that the frames are
  wireframe chrome, not a dark-mode decision, and the canvas should be
  paper-white per the deck. Confirm with Christina before item 1 lands the
  background token.
- Write/Record as the post-draw fork (Daily Prompt Blank.png) is cleaner than
  our draw -> caption -> channels chain. Theirs wins, but Record is scope-gated
  (section 4 flag).
- Our data-driven tool restriction seam is better than hardcoding the reduced
  set. Keep our mechanism, feed it their constraints.
- Their 280-char story cap vs our 80-char caption. Take 280; it is on the frame
  twice.
- The deck mascot (purple blob creature, p1 Home) appears in no Figma frame and
  no POC screen. Park it; ask whether it is brand-canon or deck garnish.
